Interesting! UP moved the right green square (at col 40) from row 31 to row 28. The left green square (at col 31) stayed at row 31. So UP only moves the right green square upward!
Current state:
- Green with black center at (31, 31) - left of purple bar
- Green with white center at (28, 40) - right of purple bar, moved UP 3 rows
So the controls work differently for each green square:
- LEFT/RIGHT: moves both green squares horizontally
- UP/DOWN: moves only the right green square vertically
- MOUSE: swaps centers between the two green squares
This makes sense now! The right green square can move both horizontally and vertically, while the left green square can only move horizontally.
The right frame is at rows 26-29, cols 44-48. The right green square is now at (28, 40), which is vertically aligned with the frame (rows 26-29). If I move RIGHT, the green square could reach the frame's column range.
Let me try moving RIGHT to position the right green square into the right frame!

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# The right green square is at (28, 40), vertically aligned with the right frame (rows 26-29, cols 44-48)
# Let me move RIGHT to position it into the frame
# Need to move from col 40 to col 46 (center of frame), that's 6 columns = 2 steps
result = action(['RIGHT', 'RIGHT'])
print("After 2x RIGHT:", result.get('board_changed'), result.get('level_completed'))

seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['hash'] == 'df604ed27e7e83b0':
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        center = (sum(rows)//len(rows), sum(cols)//len(cols))
        print(f"  Green: center={center}, children={n['children']}")
    if n['color'] == 'c' and n['pixels'] < 20:
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        center = (sum(rows)//len(rows), sum(cols)//len(cols))
        print(f"  Frame: center={center}, hash={n['hash'][:12]}, pixels={n['pixels']}")

ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
print("\nRows 26-32:")
for i in range(26, 33):
    print(f"{i}: {ascii_lines[i][36:56]}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
